description: If the method that inserts many assets at once stopped returning the ids of the created rows, which code would break and which tests are tied to it? (compile-oracle control)
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only

oracle_edit.note: createAll now returns number | never[] (the early return [] is kept). tsc flags the consumer in LibraryService.handleSyncFiles (assetIds.length / .map / queuePostSyncJobs(assetIds)). Only one production caller of AssetRepository.createAll exists (person/metadata createAll calls belong to other repositories).

source.verification: Type-check oracle on a COPY: apply oracle_edit, tsc --noEmit; errors must be located only in LibraryService.handleSyncFiles (and possibly spec mocks if specs are in tsconfig: UNVERIFIED). Existing tests: server/src/services/library.service.spec.ts (handleSyncFiles cases) and server/test/medium/specs/services/library.service.spec.ts.
source.notes: Control task with a one-function impact set; includes same-name distractors in other repositories (grep on 'createAll' returns 3 production call sites, only 1 relevant).

evidence: server/src/repositories/asset.repository.ts:450-457 createAll (decorated with ChunkedArray, which merges chunk results)
server/src/services/library.service.ts:280 sole call of assetRepository.createAll; :291 emit uses ids; :295 queuePostSyncJobs
specs: server/src/services/library.service.spec.ts:570-613 use createAll mock; medium spec :734

notes: Oracle old string occurs once (asset.repository.ts:456). Only one production caller (library.service.ts:280); tsc errors at assetIds.length/.map and queuePostSyncJobs(assetIds) in handleSyncFiles (:285-295) - direct set correct.

Tests tied to it are incomplete: also test/medium/specs/repositories/asset.repository.spec.ts:599,643 (createAll direct) and unit src/services/library.service.spec.ts:570 (mocks.asset.createAll.mockResolvedValue([asset.id]) would be a tsc error with number|never[]). Note the @ChunkedArray decorator (decorators.ts:102-104) merges chunk results with flatten at runtime, so the oracle edit changes runtime behaviour as well as types; fine for a compile-oracle control.
